To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sesame protein isolate was prepared by alkali extraction and ethanol precipitation.

the protein content of sesame seed was found to 47.70%; the protein solubility of sesame protein was affected by pH and/or NaC1 concentration; the protein isolate was highly viscoelastic; the protein isolate had high emulsion and foam stability; the protein isolate showed good water- and fat-holding capacities; and the protein isolate had low bulk density.
the protein content of sesame seeds is high, the minimum protein solubilization is at pH 5, and emulsifying capacity and foaming capacity were greatly affected by salt concentration and pH levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of pH and/or salt on the protein solubility and some functional properties of sesame seeds.
the effect of pH and salt concentration on the functional properties of sesame proteins.
the development of a functional food product based on sesame protein isolate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sesame seed protein isolate is highly viscous and has high emulsion stability, foam stability, oil holding capacity, water holding capacity and dispersability.
sesame seed protein isolate has good emulsifying, foaming and oil holding capacities.
sesame proteins are highly functional and their functionality can be manipulated to suit the needs of food industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sesame proteins are highly soluble in alkaline medium, and their emulsifying and foaming capacities and stability are greatly affected by pH and salt concentrations.

the sesame protein isolate can be used in the food industry to produce a variety of products such as bakery products, confectionary, beverages and dairy products, and also in the production of protein supplements.
sesame seed proteins are highly functional and their properties could be controlled by pH and NaCl concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sesame seed proteins can be used as an alternative source of protein in the food industry.
the functional properties of sesame protein isolate are highly dependent on the pH and salt concentration.
the protein isolate can be a good candidate for use in food products.
